title: A functor commuting with countable products commutes with derived limits

core_obligations: Existence (proof lines 2295-2300): the derived functor exists because the source category has enough K-injectives by the cited embedding theorem.

The computation (proof lines 2300-2312): the derived functor is computed by applying the functor to a K-injective representative, and products in the derived category are computed termwise by the cited results, so the assumption that the functor commutes with countable products transfers to the derived limits.
Conclusion (proof lines 2312-2316): combining the two descriptions gives that the derived functor commutes with derived limits, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Note that the derived functor exists by enough K-injectives.
Compute it on a K-injective representative and use that derived products are termwise.
Transfer the commutativity with countable products to derived limits.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an additive functor from a Grothendieck abelian category to an abelian category with exact countable products, commuting with countable products, has a derived functor commuting with derived limits (statement lines 2282-2293). The proof is a complete argument: the derived functor exists by the existence of K-injective resolutions (proof lines 2295-2300); it is computed by evaluating on a K-injective representative, and products in the derived category are computed termwise, so the commutation with countable products passes to the derived level (proof lines 2300-2312); and the two descriptions together give the assertion (proof lines 2312-2316). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two computations of the product. The claim is H2.
